sources: UCLA Samueli, SEASnet, Residential Life, Housing, CPO, HumTech, SSC, Luskin, LS Core, UCLA Recreation, ASUCLA, Transfer Student Center, Hammer Museum and Botanical Garden pages, plus BruinLife and Daily Bruin write-ups for the outdoor spots

spaces.access: UCLA students, faculty and staff; physical BruinCard for CLICC loans
spaces.description: Main undergraduate library. Quiet reading rooms on the 2nd floor (Main Reading Room, Rose Gilbert Reading Room), the 1st-floor Study Hall, six bookable group study rooms, the CLICC Lab and wēpa printing. The Study Hall stays open overnight as Night Powell.

spaces.access: Physical BruinCard only: current UCLA students, faculty and staff (Law, Anderson and UCLA Health cards accepted). Screenshots are not accepted.
spaces.description: Overnight study in Powell's 1st-floor Study Hall after the library closes; every other floor is closed. Two wēpa printers, a scanner, the six group study rooms and the CLICC lockers stay available. No staffed services.
spaces.hours_note: Overnight hours vary on weekends and holidays.

spaces.access: Active UCLA students, faculty and staff; physical BruinCard shown at the door and for any loan
spaces.description: Drop-in collaborative study and computing space for 100+ students on Powell's 1st floor: MacBook, iPad and Chromebook lending, wēpa printing, scanners, adapters and chargers, plus three bookable single-person Loop Booths.

spaces.access: UCLA students, faculty and staff with BruinCard; check in at the front desk for a room
spaces.description: Media viewing stations, first-come study cubicles and small bookable quiet rooms for 1 to 4 people on Powell's 2nd floor, across from the circulation desk. Closed weekends, breaks and holidays.

spaces.access: Reading Room open to all; group rooms and equipment lending need a BruinCard
spaces.description: Main research library on north campus. 1st-floor Reading Room with outlets and a scanner, the Research Commons with bookable group study rooms, the Garden Commons on the A-level with outlets and a printer, Café 451 by the entrance, and free day-use lockers.

spaces.access: UCLA students, faculty, staff and researchers
spaces.description: Richard C. Rudolph East Asian Library on the 2nd floor of YRL: Chinese, Japanese and Korean collections with computers, printing and research help.

spaces.access: UCLA students, orgs, staff and faculty for university-related work; no personal projects. Submit a request first.
spaces.hours_note: By request or appointment; no drop-in hours are posted.
spaces.description: The UCLA Library makerspace: MakerBot 3D printers and Artec 3D scanners in YRL's Research Commons, and an Epilog laser cutter plus Formlabs resin and Lulzbot printers in Powell 331. Little or no cost.

spaces.access: UCLA students, faculty and staff; the STEM Collaborative Learning Center needs a BruinCard
spaces.description: Engineering and physical sciences library on Boelter's 8th floor: the Learning Commons (8270) and Research Commons (8251) with the STEM Collaborative Learning Center (dual-screen desktops, wall monitors for laptops, whiteboards), laptop lending, printing and a bookable group study room (8251A).

spaces.access: UCLA students, faculty and staff
spaces.description: Quiet reading room and stacks in the Geology Building with laptop lending, printing and two bookable group study rooms (4697A for 8, 4697B for 4).

spaces.access: UCLA students, faculty and staff
spaces.description: Louise M. Darling Biomedical Library in the Center for the Health Sciences: study space, computers, laptop lending, printing, a bookable main-floor group study room (12-077E) and the Collaboration Hub upstairs. Hosts the 24-hour Biomedical Study Commons.

spaces.access: Regular library hours: any current UCLA student, faculty or staff. After hours: BruinCard swipe for graduate students in Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing, Public Health and the Life Sciences division only.
spaces.description: 24-hour quiet study commons reached from the 8th stack level of the Biomedical Library during regular hours (after-hours entrance at CHS 32-001). Bookable rooms inside are for groups only; food and drink allowed if you clean up.

spaces.access: UCLA students, faculty and staff in groups of 2 or more; check in at the service desk with your reservation
spaces.description: Group-only study rooms with whiteboards (3 to 15 people) and a 20-seat presentation space on the 6th floor of CHS.

spaces.access: UCLA students, faculty and staff
spaces.description: Art, architecture, film and design library on the 1st floor of the Public Affairs Building. The 5th-floor reading room is reserved for quiet study, with carrels and tables. Computers, laptop lending and printing.

spaces.access: UCLA students and staff, and the public
spaces.description: Walter H. Rubsamen Music Library off the Schoenberg atrium. The Reading Room is the main quiet study space, the classroom is quiet study when no class is in it, and the 20-seat Seminar Room is bookable for groups of 7 to 20. Computers, laptop lending, printing.

spaces.access: 3rd-floor study areas open to all UCLA; the 1st, 2nd and 4th floors, group rooms and labs are Anderson-only (Anderson BruinCard)
spaces.description: Anderson School library in Entrepreneurs Hall. Non-Anderson students can use the 3rd-floor study areas and one public workstation; the group study rooms, computing labs, pods and the whole 4th floor are for Anderson students.

spaces.access: UCLA Law students and UCLA faculty/staff with BruinCard. Other UCLA students must reserve a study space online in advance (ucla.edu email) and show a BruinCard; access can be suspended during law finals.
spaces.description: Hugh & Hazel Darling Law Library: big reading rooms on the 1st floor, the Tower Reading Room on the 4th (law students only), public computers and a wēpa kiosk. Non-law students book entry on the Law Library's own site.

spaces.hours_note: Open during the academic quarter only; closed finals week, breaks and university holidays.
spaces.access: All UCLA Engineering students, free. Student staff train you on each machine before you use it.
spaces.description: 9,000 sq ft engineering makerspace: Prusa 3D printer farm, laser cutters, light machining tools, PCB printers, a reflow oven, electronics test gear, an embroidery machine and VR, supervised by trained student staff.

spaces.access: Engineering students, faculty and staff; staffed by machinists who instruct and supervise
spaces.description: General metal machining shop (mills, lathes, drill presses, band saws) run by UCLA Samueli Shop Services. Submit an online machine shop request.

spaces.access: All UCLA students, on or off campus, free. Technicians show you the machines; the wood and metal zone needs extra training.
spaces.description: Residential Life's 3,000 sq ft makerspace: a 3D printing and laser cutting hub, a soft-goods zone (sewing, embroidery), a woodshop and metalworking zone, and general workspace.

spaces.access: All UCLA students, on or off campus
spaces.description: Residential Life learning center with two 20-seat study labs, lounge seating with outlets and two wēpa printers (B&W and color). Open to every UCLA student, not just residents.

spaces.text: De Neve Labs (De Neve Commons P333)
spaces.access: All UCLA students, on or off campus
spaces.description: Residential Life learning center on the 3rd floor of De Neve Commons: a computer lab, a music production studio, lounge seating with outlets and two wēpa printers.

spaces.access: UCLA Housing residents (it is the housing tech help desk); the lab is open for use
spaces.description: Housing's tech center in Covel Commons: eight Windows PCs with Office, B&W and color printing, copying, scanning and computer repair.

spaces.hours_note: Closed university holidays. Monday 8 to 10 AM is maintenance. 3760 and 4404 can be reserved for classes.
spaces.access: SEASnet account (students in engineering courses); coursework has priority
spaces.description: About 200 Windows workstations across five Boelter labs for engineering coursework. BruinPrint printer in 2664.

spaces.hours_note: Hours are on pic.ucla.edu, which was unreachable when this list was built.
spaces.access: Students enrolled in PIC classes and Math students (PIC account)
spaces.description: Program in Computing lab on the 2nd floor of the Math Sciences building, for PIC and math coursework.

spaces.hours_note: Walk in whenever no class is scheduled in the room. Closed university holidays.
spaces.access: Students enrolled in a Social Sciences course and Social Sciences grad students (account is created when you first log in)
spaces.description: About 155 Windows workstations with statistical and GIS software across three Public Affairs labs. Printing 10¢ a side with a quarterly subsidy for eligible undergrads.

spaces.hours_note: Closed between quarters, in summer and on university holidays.
spaces.access: Luskin School students, faculty and staff only
spaces.description: Windows lab with ArcGIS, SPSS, Stata, SAS, R, AutoCAD and Adobe Creative Suite. Not open for general UCLA use.

spaces.hours_note: Classes and exams booked in the room take priority; check the lab calendar for free-use hours.
spaces.access: Any student during open hours, no reservation needed
spaces.description: Humanities Technology lab with 30 MacBooks to borrow in the room, a color printer for enrolled classes and an instructional 3D printer. Drop in to study, take an exam or borrow a laptop.

spaces.access: Students registered in Life Sciences or Physical Sciences classes
spaces.description: LS Core computing lab for LIFESCI coursework. Printing 5¢ a page, billed to BAR.

spaces.hours_note: CPO Study Hall (8:30 PM to midnight, Mon to Thu) runs weeks 2 through finals, with a free ride home if you study at least an hour.
spaces.access: All UCLA students, free
spaces.description: Community Programs Office lab in the Student Activities Center with free printing (150 duplex prints a quarter). The Basic Needs lounge next door in suite 121 has café seating, microwaves, lockers and the Food Closet.

spaces.text: Ackerman Union open study rooms (2nd & 3rd floor)
spaces.access: UCLA students, faculty and staff
spaces.description: Any unreserved meeting room on Ackerman's 2nd and 3rd floors is open for studying; the day's schedule is posted next to each door. The food court is one floor down.

spaces.access: Open to the public
spaces.description: The student union: 1st-floor food court seating, the outdoor Wescom Student Terrace over Bruin Plaza, the Bruin Viewpoint study lounge on the A-level next to the A-level restaurants, and lounges on the 2nd and 3rd floors.

spaces.access: UCLA students
spaces.description: Small ASUCLA lounge with bright lighting and couches right beside Kerckhoff Coffee House.

spaces.access: UCLA students
spaces.description: The larger of the two Kerckhoff lounges: a co-ed lounge with comfortable couch seating.

spaces.access: Open to the public
spaces.description: Historic brick-and-stained-glass café that fills with students studying over coffee; the patio outside has shaded tables and a view of Bruin Walk.

spaces.hours_note: Summer: Mon to Thu 10 AM to 2 PM.
spaces.access: UCLA students; built for transfer, commuter and non-traditional students
spaces.description: Lounge to hang out, study and meet other transfers, on the ground floor of Kerckhoff.

spaces.access: UCLA students (gym and pool need a BruinCard or Rec membership)
spaces.description: Home of the Community Programs Office, the Bruin Resource Center, student org offices, a gym and a pool. Lobbies and hallways get used for studying; the CPO lab and Basic Needs lounge are in suite 121.

spaces.access: UCLA students with BruinCard. BruinHub study pods need a quarterly passholder application.
spaces.description: BruinHub on the 2nd floor is a space for commuter and housing-insecure students with study tables, charging stations, a microwave, fridge, lockers and study pods. The 2nd-floor succulent garden has umbrella tables over Bruin Walk.

spaces.text: Lu Valle Commons & Jimmy’s Coffee House
spaces.access: Open to the public
spaces.description: North campus food hall next to the Law School with Peet's coffee at Jimmy's, several restaurants and indoor and outdoor seating. Busy at lunch.

spaces.access: Open to the public
spaces.description: Café with paninis, soup and poke bowls near Bunche Hall and the Sculpture Garden, with a little fireplace for chilly days.

spaces.access: Open to the public
spaces.description: South campus food court one level below the Court of Sciences, between Boelter, Young and Boyer, with Peet's Coffee, indoor tables and outdoor seating. Busy at lunch.

spaces.access: Open to the public
spaces.description: Peet's café at the entrance of YRL. Seating spills into the library's 1st-floor commons, which has outlets and a printer.

spaces.access: Open to the public
spaces.description: Peet's café at the Gonda Research Center on south campus with indoor and outdoor seating; quieter than the central cafés.

spaces.access: Open to the public
spaces.description: Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf café in the Anderson complex with shaded outdoor seating, next to the Rosenfeld Library.

spaces.access: Open to the public
spaces.description: Small café in the Ostin Music Center beside the Music Library.

spaces.hours_note: No hours are posted; follows Engineering VI building access.
spaces.access: Not posted (engineering building)
spaces.description: Patio between Engineering V and VI shaded by the surrounding buildings, with benches, tables and plants, plus an indoor lounge with comfy seating, movable chairs and a TV for group work. Take the elevator to 3.

spaces.hours_note: No hours are posted; follows Boelter Hall access.
spaces.access: Not posted
spaces.description: Open rooftop above the Science and Engineering Library with awnings for shade and restrooms. Quiet and rarely crowded. No outlets.

spaces.access: Open to the public
spaces.description: Wooden outdoor tables with power outlets at the base of the Math Sciences building, near Boelter and the Court of Sciences Student Center.

spaces.hours_note: No hours are posted; follows building access.
spaces.access: Not posted
spaces.description: Elevated patio with a shade structure and tables looking toward Powell and Kaplan Hall. Low foot traffic, no outlets.

spaces.hours_note: No hours are posted; follows building access.
spaces.access: Not posted
spaces.description: White balcony on Broad's top floor with south-facing views toward Santa Monica. Quiet, no outlets.

spaces.hours_note: No hours are posted; follows building access.
spaces.access: Not posted
spaces.description: Study and lounge areas with outlets overlooking the Inverted Fountain, for solo or group work. Popular with psych majors.

spaces.hours_note: No hours are posted; follows building access.
spaces.access: Not posted
spaces.description: Compact, tucked-away lounge in the School of Education with whiteboards; good for long solo or group sessions.

spaces.access: Open to the public
spaces.description: Five-acre lawn and brick plaza with 70+ sculptures between Broad, Bunche and YRL. Lawn seating, coral-tree shade, no outlets. Café 451 and Northern Lights are a short walk.

spaces.hours_note: November to January it closes at 4 PM. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas.
spaces.access: Open to the public, free
spaces.description: Seven-acre garden on the southeast edge of campus with benches tucked into leafy nooks, wooden tables, a stream and a bamboo grove. Very quiet, no outlets.

spaces.access: Open to the public
spaces.description: The main quad between Royce, Powell, Haines and Kaplan, plus the shady fig and sycamore lawns of Dickson Court North and South just east of it. Benches and grass only, lots of foot traffic. Powell and Kerckhoff Coffee House are steps away.

spaces.access: Not posted (open courtyard)
spaces.description: Well-furnished courtyard shaded by evergreens and lit by string lights in the evening, next to Lu Valle Commons.

spaces.access: Open to the public, free admission
spaces.description: Half-indoor, half-outdoor museum courtyard in Westwood Village, a short walk south of campus, with outlets for laptops and the Lulu café. Quiet on weekdays.
